claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has acceptable room-temperature tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr suffers rapid oxygen uptake and pesting during high-temperature exposure.
Pack cementation aluminizing will deposit a thin aluminide coating on equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminide coating will transform upon high-temperature oxidation into a continuous Al2O3 scale.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be slow-growing.
During high-temperature air exposure, the aluminide layer will oxidize preferentially.
A continuous Al2O3 scale will retard further oxygen ingress into the alloy.
Retarding oxygen ingress will mitigate the rapid oxidation that compromises alloy performance.
Aluminized specimens will have lower oxidation rates than untreated specimens.
The lower oxidation rate will be indicated by reduced weight gain.
Aluminized specimens will develop a more uniform oxide layer than untreated specimens.
Aluminized specimens will maintain their original room-temperature ductility.
Aluminized specimens will maintain their original high-temperature yield strength.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr oxidizes rapidly and undergoes pesting under approximately 800 °C air exposure for 5 hours.
Rapid oxidation of untreated material prevents preservation of its mechanical properties.
The proposed protection is applicable to air exposure at approximately 800 °C for 5 hours.
The short-term effectiveness of aluminizing over a 5-hour exposure is anticipated based on prior related studies.
Long-term scale performance under extended exposure and varying mechanical loads is uncertain.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant oxidation reduction relative to untreated controls would falsify the hypothesis.
Significant mechanical-property degradation in aluminized specimens relative to untreated controls would falsify the hypothesis.
